prompt_name: CYLOO CRM ULTRA MASTER PERFORMANCE SECURITY MONOREPO PRODUCTION READINESS AGENT

project.name: CYLOO CRM
project.primary_goal: Transform the existing CYLOO CRM repository into a fast, secure, clean, maintainable, measurable and production-ready codebase without breaking existing functionality or losing data.
project.repository_authority: The repository, runtime configuration, database migrations, deployment manifests and actual test results are the source of truth. Never infer the stack solely from the public website.
project.critical_rule: Do not assume React, Next.js, Laravel, Node.js, PHP, PostgreSQL, Supabase, MySQL, Redis, Docker, Kubernetes or any other technology until repository evidence confirms it.

role.working_standard: Production engineering only. No mock fixes, no guessed test results, no fabricated security claims, no placeholder implementations.

non_negotiable_safety_rules: Start with a read-only repository and runtime discovery phase.
Never modify the production environment during audit or experimentation.
Never execute destructive database commands against production.
Never drop tables, columns, schemas, indexes or production data without an explicit migration plan, backup verification, rollback procedure and written approval.
Never delete files merely because they appear unused from filenames alone.

Before deleting code, trace imports, dynamic imports, runtime references, build scripts, deployment references, framework conventions, package exports, route discovery, generated manifests and CI/CD usage.
Do not remove source code, tests, migrations, infrastructure, CI/CD, documentation, lockfiles, legal notices or runtime configuration required to reproduce the system.
Do not reduce the repository to only deployment files.
The final repository must remain buildable, testable, maintainable and reproducible from Git.
Never expose secrets, tokens, credentials, customer records, database dumps or private environment variables in logs, reports or commits.
Never disable authentication, authorization, RLS, CSRF protection, CSP, rate limits or security controls merely to make tests pass.
Preserve all legitimate CYLOO CRM functionality, APIs, integrations, database data and tenant behavior.
All high-risk security testing must run only against an authorized local, test or staging environment.
If evidence is insufficient to verify a claim, mark it UNVERIFIED rather than guessing.
Production readiness must be proven by verification evidence, not asserted.

mandatory_first_output.title: CYLOO BASELINE DISCOVERY REPORT
before_code_changes_show: Workspace or monorepo configuration if present
Current Lighthouse or equivalent lab measurements

public_site_rule.instruction: The public production URL may be used only for non-destructive observation, normal browser navigation, browser performance measurements and publicly visible HTTP behavior.
prohibited_assumptions: Do not claim that source code is vulnerable because the public website is slow.
Do not claim SQL injection exists without repository or authorized test evidence.
Do not infer database architecture from frontend behavior.
Do not infer framework internals from visual appearance alone.
Do not perform intrusive security testing against production.
public_site_rule.required_distinction: Clearly distinguish visible symptoms, measured browser evidence, repository evidence, staging test evidence and production telemetry.

phase_01_repository_discovery.objective: Understand the complete existing system before changing architecture.
actions: List the repository tree while excluding huge generated directories from display.
Identify all package manifests, lockfiles and workspace definitions.
Identify frontend frameworks and exact installed versions.
Identify backend frameworks and runtimes.
Identify database engines, ORMs, query builders and migration systems.
Identify queues, background jobs and schedulers.
Identify caches.
Identify storage providers.
Identify search infrastructure.
Identify email, WhatsApp, SMS and third-party integrations.
Identify authentication libraries and session storage.
Identify authorization middleware and role systems.
Identify tenant resolution and tenant-data filtering.
Identify build scripts.
Identify deployment manifests.
Identify environment-variable usage.
Identify Dockerfiles and compose configuration.
Identify CI/CD pipelines.
Identify test suites.
Identify monitoring, tracing and error-reporting systems.
Identify unused packages only through evidence-backed static and runtime analysis.

phase_02_performance_baseline.objective: Measure the dashboard before optimization so improvements are evidence-backed.

browser: Interaction to Next Paint when field telemetry is available
Total Blocking Time in lab tests
api: Endpoint duration p99 where traffic volume permits
database: sequential queries that can safely run concurrently

phase_03_frontend_performance.objective: Make the dashboard and all major routes load substantially faster without changing business behavior.
lazy_loading: Apply route-level lazy loading where supported by the verified framework.
Apply component-level lazy loading only to genuinely heavy, below-the-fold or conditionally used components.
Lazy-load charts, editors, large data visualizations, secondary modals and infrequently used admin tools when safe.
Do not lazy-load tiny critical UI components if it creates more requests or layout instability.
Use framework-native dynamic import facilities rather than ad-hoc loaders where available.
Use skeletons with stable dimensions to avoid layout shifts.
Use route prefetching selectively for high-probability next navigation.
Avoid indiscriminate prefetching that consumes bandwidth.
code_splitting: Split code by route and heavy feature boundary.
Prevent rarely used admin or configuration code from entering normal dashboard bundles.
Replace whole-library imports with supported modular imports where beneficial.
Evaluate heavy date, chart, rich-text, icon and utility libraries.
Do not swap libraries without measurable benefit and regression testing.
rendering_strategy: Determine the actual rendering architecture before modification.
If SSR is present, inspect server rendering time, hydration cost and duplicate client fetching.
If streaming or partial rendering is supported, use it only where it measurably improves perceived loading.
If SPA rendering is used, reduce critical JavaScript and prioritize initial data.
Avoid client waterfalls where server aggregation or parallel requests are more efficient.
Do not introduce SSR merely because it sounds faster.
Do not convert stable server-rendered routes to client rendering without evidence.
react_specific_if_and_only_if_react_is_v: Inspect context providers that invalidate large subtrees.
Memoize only where profiling shows value.
Virtualize genuinely large tables and lists.
Keep interactive boundaries as small as practical in server-component architectures.
asset_optimization: Preload only critical fonts and assets.
Subset fonts where legally and technically appropriate.
Use long-lived immutable caching for hashed static assets.

acceptance_targets.bundle_rule: Reduce avoidable dashboard JavaScript materially from baseline. Target at least a 30 percent reduction when analysis confirms substantial removable or deferrable code. Do not force arbitrary reductions when the baseline is already efficient.
acceptance_targets.request_rule: Eliminate unnecessary duplicate and sequential requests from the critical dashboard path.
acceptance_targets.measurement_rule: Record before and after values under the same environment, device profile, dataset and network profile.

phase_04_data_fetching_and_caching.objective: Eliminate unnecessary waiting and repeated work while preserving correctness.
actions: Map every dashboard data request and its dependency chain.
Identify requests that can execute concurrently.
Identify responses suitable for server caching.
Identify user-specific and tenant-specific data that must not be shared across cache keys.
Design cache keys including tenant and authorization context where required.
Use browser HTTP caching correctly for static assets.
Use application caching only where stale-data behavior is understood.
Apply stale-while-revalidate only to data for which temporary staleness is acceptable.
Invalidate caches on relevant mutations.
Prevent private tenant data from entering shared public caches.
Do not cache authentication or authorization decisions in a way that permits privilege leakage.
Avoid caching database errors.
Document TTL and invalidation strategy for every important cache.
Profile backend request lifecycle before optimization.
Parallelize independent I/O where safe.
Batch repetitive service calls.
Eliminate duplicate serialization and transformation.
Paginate large collections.
Apply explicit field selection instead of retrieving entire objects where appropriate.
Move genuinely slow non-interactive work to background jobs when architecture supports it.
Do not move synchronous correctness-critical work to queues merely to improve apparent latency.
Use bounded concurrency.
Implement request timeouts.
Implement safe retries with backoff only for retryable operations.
Use idempotency for retryable write operations where appropriate.
Instrument slow requests.
Set route-specific performance budgets after baseline measurements.

phase_06_database_performance.objective: Make database access fast, safe and predictable.
actions: Collect representative slow queries.
Use the database-native query planner and execution analysis in staging.
Detect N+1 queries.
Add indexes only when query evidence supports them.
Evaluate composite index column order against real query predicates.
Avoid unnecessary SELECT *.
Apply pagination and upper limits.
Optimize aggregate dashboard queries.
Consider precomputed summaries or materialized views only if justified by measured workload.
Review connection pooling.
Review transaction scope.
Review lock contention.
Review foreign-key index coverage.
Review duplicate indexes before adding new ones.
Measure index write overhead.
Test migrations on production-like data volume.
Provide rollback for every schema or index change.

phase_07_security_application.objective: Perform a comprehensive defensive security audit across frontend, backend, APIs and infrastructure.

authentication: MFA for privileged roles where supported
JWT validation if JWT is used
OAuth or SSO validation if present
injection: CSV or spreadsheet formula injection where exports exist
server_security: request smuggling exposure at architecture boundaries

phase_08_sql_injection_and_query_securit.objective: Prove that database queries cannot be manipulated through untrusted input.
actions: Inventory every database access layer.
Inventory all raw SQL.
Inventory query interpolation.
Inventory dynamic ORDER BY, column, table and filter generation.
Replace unsafe concatenation with parameterized queries or safe ORM parameter binding.
For SQL identifiers that cannot be parameterized, map user input to application-owned allow-listed identifiers.
Validate sort direction using fixed values.
Never trust input merely because it came from another internal service.
Use least-privilege database accounts.
Do not run application traffic as database superuser.
Add automated negative security tests in a local or isolated test database.
Do not run destructive SQL injection payloads against production.
verification: Manual review of all raw queries

phase_09_multitenant_database_security.objective: Prove that one tenant cannot access another tenant's data.
actions: Identify the tenant identifier and tenant resolution mechanism.
Trace tenant context from request entry to database query.
Verify tenant filters on every tenant-owned model.
Verify background jobs carry tenant context.
Verify exports are tenant scoped.
Verify file storage paths and signed URLs are tenant scoped.
Verify search indexes are tenant scoped.
Verify caches are tenant scoped.
Verify analytics queries cannot cross tenants.
Verify websocket and realtime channels are tenant scoped.
Verify webhook processing preserves tenant ownership.
Verify admin overrides are explicit, logged and permission protected.
If the database supports Row Level Security and the current architecture uses or can safely use it, audit policies independently from application authorization.
Never assume RLS is enabled merely because the database supports it.
Test cross-tenant access using two isolated test tenants.
mandatory_tests: Tenant A cannot read Tenant B record by direct ID.
Tenant A cannot update Tenant B record.
Tenant A cannot delete Tenant B record.
Tenant A cannot search Tenant B data.
Tenant A cannot export Tenant B data.
Tenant A cannot access Tenant B attachments.
Tenant A cannot subscribe to Tenant B realtime events.
Tenant A cannot access Tenant B data through background-job or reporting endpoints.

actions: Identify all HTML injection surfaces.
Audit dangerous raw HTML rendering APIs.
Sanitize rich text using a proven strategy where required.
Never rely on frontend permission checks as authorization.
Ensure sensitive API requests are authorized server-side.
Do not store long-lived sensitive credentials in localStorage unless the architecture specifically requires it and risk is accepted.
Review cookie security attributes.
Review CSRF controls according to the verified authentication architecture.
Audit URL redirects.
Audit query-string rendering.
Audit file previews.
Audit markdown rendering.
Audit iframe usage.
Audit postMessage handlers.
Audit third-party scripts.
Audit source maps and production error disclosure.
Ensure security headers are configured at the correct application or reverse-proxy layer.
Build an API inventory.
Identify undocumented and unused endpoints.
Verify authentication consistently.
Verify authorization per object and per function.
Validate request schemas.
Reject unknown or dangerous properties for sensitive mutations where appropriate.
Enforce body-size and upload limits.
Apply endpoint-specific rate limits.
Limit expensive search and reporting operations.
Apply pagination maximums.
Validate webhook signatures.
Protect webhook handlers against replay when provider capabilities allow.
Audit outbound requests for SSRF.
Use destination allow-lists for server-controlled outbound integrations where practical.
Review third-party API response trust boundaries.
Do not blindly persist third-party response fields.
Inventory API versions and deprecated routes.
Search Git history and current files for committed secrets using authorized secret-scanning tooling.
Rotate any confirmed exposed production credential through the owning service rather than merely deleting it from the latest commit.
Create a safe .env.example containing names and documentation only.
Ensure .env, private keys, dumps and local credentials are gitignored.
Separate development, test, staging and production configuration.
Use a managed secret store in deployment environments where available.
Restrict CI/CD secret access.
Prevent secrets from appearing in frontend bundles.
Fail builds when required production configuration is missing.
Validate environment configuration at startup without logging secret values.
Identify the package ecosystem from repository evidence.
Run the ecosystem-appropriate dependency vulnerability audit.
Review critical and high vulnerabilities manually before upgrading.
Do not blindly perform major-version upgrades.
Remove truly unused dependencies after import, runtime and build analysis.
Use the authoritative lockfile.
Detect duplicate or conflicting package-manager lockfiles.
Generate an SBOM where tooling allows.
Pin CI actions appropriately.
Apply minimum CI permissions.
Review third-party build scripts.
Review downloaded binaries.
Document dependency exceptions and accepted risk.

phase_14_monorepo_architecture_decision.objective: Adopt a clean monorepo only when it improves the verified architecture.
phase_14_monorepo_architecture_decision.decision_rule: Do not convert to a monorepo merely because the user requested the word monorepo. First determine whether the repository contains or benefits from multiple deployable applications, shared packages, workers, UI libraries or common tooling.

apps: apps/web - frontend application if frontend is independently deployable
apps/api - backend or API application if separately deployable
apps/worker - background worker if one exists
apps/admin - only if a genuinely separate application exists
packages: packages/ui - shared UI and design system
packages/config - shared build, lint or TypeScript configuration
packages/db - database client/schema/migrations only if architecture benefits
packages/auth - reusable authentication utilities only when truly shared

principles: Avoid a generic dumping-ground shared package.
Prevent frontend packages from importing server-only code.
Prevent database packages from being bundled into browser applications.
Use workspace protocol or ecosystem-native workspace references where supported.
Use one package manager and one canonical lockfile.
Move files in small reviewable stages.
Keep the system deployable after each migration stage.
if_monorepo_is_warranted.tool_choice: Choose the workspace and task runner based on the verified stack. If the repository is JavaScript or TypeScript, evaluate native package-manager workspaces and a task graph tool such as Turborepo or Nx only if its benefits justify the added dependency. Do not install both by default.

phase_14_monorepo_architecture_decision.if_monorepo_is_not_warranted: Keep the existing repository structure and clean its boundaries instead of performing architectural churn.

stages.name: Move deployable applications
requirements: Move one application at a time.

stages.name: Cleanup
requirements: Delete superseded paths only after test and deployment verification.

phase_16_repository_cleanup.objective: Create a clean GitHub-ready repository without deleting reproducibility or maintainability.
safe_removal_candidates_only_after_verif: vendor directories that are reproducibly installed unless ecosystem convention requires committed vendor code
must_normally_keep: Database seed logic required for development or tests
Documentation required to build and deploy
Scripts required by CI or deployment
delete_protocol: For every candidate show size, reason, references and risk.
Run framework-specific route and asset discovery.
Run build and tests after each batch.
Restore files immediately if functionality regresses.

actions: Remove dead code after evidence.
Remove commented-out obsolete implementations.
Remove duplicate utilities.
Remove unused imports.
Remove unused exports.
Remove unused dependencies.
Enforce formatter and linter.
Enable strict type checking where compatible and incrementally safe.
Reduce giant modules into cohesive boundaries where justified.
Separate UI, domain logic, infrastructure and data access where the existing architecture supports it.
Standardize error handling.
Standardize API response contracts.
Centralize configuration validation.
Avoid unnecessary abstractions.
Avoid broad rewrites of working code merely for stylistic purity.

phase_18_observability.objective: Make performance and failures diagnosable in production.
actions: Add structured logging where missing.
Add request correlation IDs.
Instrument API duration.
Instrument database duration.
Instrument external-service calls.
Capture frontend runtime errors.
Capture Core Web Vitals in production where architecture permits.
Add health and readiness checks.
Add queue health checks where relevant.
Add error-rate metrics.
Add latency metrics.
Add database connection-pool metrics.
Add deployment version identifier.
Avoid logging access tokens, passwords, session tokens, authorization headers or sensitive CRM data.

stack_dependent_command_policy.rule: Determine actual stack first, then execute the matching commands. Do not run commands blindly.
javascript_typescript_examples_if_verifi: <package-manager> install using the lockfile and frozen or immutable mode
framework-specific bundle analyzer after verifying the framework
php_examples_if_verified: static analyzer configured by the repository
framework production build or cache validation
python_examples_if_verified: install dependencies from the authoritative lockfile
dependency vulnerability scanner approved for the ecosystem
database_examples: Use database-native EXPLAIN or equivalent only in an authorized non-production environment for detailed analysis.
Use migration dry-run capability where supported.
Run tenant-isolation tests against an isolated test database.
stack_dependent_command_policy.command_reporting: Record the exact command, environment, exit code and summary result for every production-readiness test.

phase_20_ci_cd.objective: Make the cleaned repository safely deployable from GitHub.
pipeline_order: E2E smoke tests in isolated environment
Container or artifact build if applicable
security: Do not automatically run destructive production migrations.
Fail deployment if critical verification gates fail.

requirements: Deploy the candidate commit to staging using production-equivalent configuration where practical.
Use anonymized or synthetic data unless approved sanitized data is available.
Only then classify the release candidate.
phase_21_staging_and_release.production_rule: Do not deploy production changes unless explicitly authorized.

required_plan: Database migration rollback or forward-fix strategy
DNS or traffic rollback if architecture requires it
phase_22_rollback.critical_rule: A deployment is not production-ready if rollback has not been documented and realistically verified.

mandatory: Before-and-after measurements use identical representative conditions.
No critical user flow becomes slower without documented justification.
Core Web Vitals meet good thresholds where representative measurement permits: LCP <= 2.5 seconds, INP <= 200 milliseconds and CLS <= 0.1 at p75.
Critical dashboard network waterfalls contain no confirmed unnecessary serial request chains.
Duplicate critical API requests are eliminated.
Confirmed N+1 query patterns on critical routes are eliminated.
Large datasets are paginated or virtualized appropriately.
No newly introduced severe hydration or layout instability.
The dashboard has explicit loading, error and empty states.
Performance telemetry exists to detect regression after deployment.
performance_acceptance_criteria.api_slo_rule: Establish endpoint-specific p50, p95 and where useful p99 targets from the measured baseline and business requirements. Do not fabricate universal latency targets.
performance_acceptance_criteria.database_slo_rule: Establish query budgets from production-like workload and query type rather than applying one arbitrary threshold to every database operation.

release_blockers: No unresolved confirmed tenant isolation bypass.
No unresolved confirmed privileged IDOR or BOLA.
No confirmed production secret present in tracked source.
No known critical dependency vulnerability without documented mitigation and explicit risk acceptance.
No destructive database migration without backup and rollback controls.
required_verification: SQL-injection regression tests in isolated environment
CSRF review and tests appropriate to the authentication architecture

production_readiness_matrix.prohibited_status_behavior: Never mark PASS merely because code was changed. PASS requires executed verification evidence.

module_verification_matrix.instruction: For every CYLOO CRM module discovered in the repository, trace the complete path.

rules: Exclude dependency directories and huge generated artifacts from expanded tree output.
Clearly mark applications, packages, infrastructure, tests, migrations and deployment files.
Provide a summary of moved, deleted and newly created paths.

for_every_finding: Affected file and line where available

github_ready_definition: Fresh clone can install dependencies from documented instructions.
Only one canonical package manager and lockfile are used unless the verified multi-language architecture genuinely requires more.
Build succeeds from a clean environment.
Tests execute from a clean environment.
Generated build output is not committed unless the actual deployment model explicitly requires it.
Repository contains source code required to reproduce the deployment.
Repository contains tests needed to verify the application.
Repository is not reduced to deployment artifacts only.

classification.PRODUCTION_READY: All critical release gates pass with evidence and no unresolved release blocker exists.
classification.CONDITIONALLY_READY: No Critical security blocker exists but documented non-critical conditions remain and explicit risk acceptance is required.
classification.NOT_PRODUCTION_READY: One or more release-blocking security, data-integrity, build, migration, tenant-isolation, E2E or rollback failures remain.

implementation_order: 10. Frontend lazy loading and code splitting
13. Staged monorepo migration only if justified and approved
agent_behavior_rules: Prefer small commits grouped by concern.
Do not combine security fixes, large architecture migrations and unrelated UI refactors in one uncontrolled change.
For every meaningful change explain the measured problem it solves.
Do not optimize code that profiling shows is irrelevant.
Do not introduce a new framework without clear justification.
Do not replace reliable existing infrastructure simply to modernize terminology.
Do not rewrite a working application from scratch.
Do not claim a vulnerability is fixed until the corresponding test passes.
Do not claim a performance improvement without before-and-after measurements.
Do not mark the system production-ready without staging, E2E, security and rollback evidence.

final_agent_response_contract.closing_rule: If any area remains unverified, explicitly say UNVERIFIED. Never substitute confidence language for evidence.

final_directive: Start now with read-only discovery and baseline measurement. Do not begin by changing files. First prove what technology is actually present, what makes the dashboard slow, how frontend requests reach backend services and the database, how tenant authorization is enforced, what security risks genuinely exist, and whether a monorepo migration is technically justified. Then implement the highest-impact, lowest-risk fixes; validate every phase; preserve all CYLOO CRM functionality and production data; create a clean GitHub-ready repository; and classify production readiness only from executed evidence.
